# RailWeave

> Open-source Rust toolkit and interoperability layer for converting railway simulator routes and rolling stock through a versioned, simulator-neutral intermediate representation (IR).

RailWeave uses a hub-and-spoke conversion architecture. Source adapters import simulator data into RailWeave IR; target adapters export that IR into simulator packages. This keeps simulator-specific work reusable across current and future sources and targets instead of coupling conversion logic to one simulator pair.

## Scope

- Railway route conversion and migration
- Train simulator format interoperability
- Rolling-stock and train metadata conversion
- Cross-simulator route and rolling-stock composition
- Deterministic conversion with provenance
- Explicit diagnostics for unsupported, inferred, defaulted, or lossy data

## Simulator ecosystems and formats

RailWeave currently covers or exposes adapter boundaries for BVE / OpenBVE, MSTS / OpenRails, Trainz, Train Simulator / RailWorks, Loksim3D, RailWeave JSON, GeoJSON, and RailWeave track CSV. OpenBVE is the first production export target.

## Extension model

New simulator support fits one of three extension points:

1. a built-in source adapter that imports a redistributable or testable format into RailWeave IR;
2. a target adapter that exports RailWeave IR into another simulator ecosystem;
3. an external adapter for proprietary, fast-moving, SDK-dependent, or game-installation-dependent formats.

The external adapter protocol is language-independent and returns the same versioned ImportResult JSON shape as built-in importers.

## Architecture and guarantees

- Versioned simulator-neutral graph IR
- Source provenance retained on imported entities
- Stable diagnostic codes for conversion loss
- Deterministic IDs, path selection, and output
- Local-only asset handling; no DRM bypass or bundled proprietary fixtures
- Hub-and-spoke adapter architecture rather than pairwise converters
